pr_body:
This PR adds support to `LightOccluder2D`s for the z index, fixes #64939 and fixes #74265. All `canvasItem`s will now receive shadows only from `LightOccluder2D`s that have a higher z index. This is achieved by passing the z index as the integer part of the shadow texture, and using a different depth check. The new depth check first compares the shadow and object z index to determine if a shadow should be cast, and later performs the normal check with only the fractional depth part.

`DirectionalLight2D`s maintain their old behavior since their depth maps can have values above or below 1 and 0, which would mess up the new depth check. The z index used by occluders is absolute, since it is not known in the lightning pass. This change also only applies to the `forward+` renderer, since the size of the `canvas.glsl` shader's push constant has been increased to 144, which some low end devices don't support. The only change that affects performance is the removal of `sampler2DShadow` in favor of a custom sampler, but the effect should be minimal. 

Here is a comparison, left being old and right new. Instead of all the shadows being overlayed on top, they now respect the layering. 

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/47889291/7aa2748d-b442-4e5d-be15-b932969096b9)

Please let me know if this is acceptable to merge and if I should do any changes, this is my first PR here. However, I believe that this is a crucial feature, as 2D lighting is currently almost unusable for me.
pr_comments:
I agree that this seems to be an valuable improvement the behaviour of light occluders. However, the way it is implemented right now won't work on mobile devices when using the Vulkan backend and it appears to not be implemented for the compatibility backend at all. 

Unfortunately, lack of mobile support is a huge problem for a PR like this, so we will need to figure out a way to implement the feature for all platforms in order to move forward. 

We typically handle culling of lights and shadows on the CPU side, so perhaps we can get away without doing the culling on the GPU.

> Unfortunately, lack of mobile support is a huge problem for a PR like this, so we will need to figure out a way to implement the feature for all platforms in order to move forward.

Makes sense. I'll see if I can add support for the other rendering engines as well. I didn't know if the approach I chose is even acceptable in the first place, since it touches the renderer shader directly, which is why I only added it to forward+ first. If it's fine I will implement it with the other back-ends as well, so just tell me.

> We typically handle culling of lights and shadows on the CPU side, so perhaps we can get away without doing the culling on the GPU.

The problem is the way that light is rendered. The shadow map gets calculated at the very end of the renderer pass, and then applied in the shader. This means that all the lights and shadows get applied at once at the end, which doesn't allow them to be rendered in order like all the normal objects.

So as far as I can see, this fix seems like a pretty good solution that doesn't involve changing the entire renderer. I could be completely wrong about this though, I've never really worked with rendering code before.

Sorry for leaving this PR dead for so long, I haven't really used Godot for a while. Recently I wanted to use it again and saw that the light issue still existed, so I came back to this and wrote a different PR with somewhat better code. It uses an entirely different approach and all of the code is new which is why I will close this one.

issue_context.title: CanvasItem light_mask is ignored by LightOccluder2D occluder_light_mask
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.0.alpha14.official [106b68050]

### System information

Ubuntu, Nvidia

### Issue description

By setting CanvasItem light_mask to a different layer than LightOccluder2D light_mask, it was possible to have shadows not being drawn on top of sprites. This does no longer work.

Godot 3:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23386940/186956411-51c6efde-cab8-45f2-a115-fdea6b1e7fb8.png)

Identical setup in Godot 4:

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/23386940/c2356ef1-f9ac-4245-9ec4-c70a65e431c4)

Especially in topdown games you generally need this to work.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Set your PointLight2D's range_item_cull_mask to cover layer 1 and 2
2. Set your Sprite2D's light_mask to 2 only
3. Add LightOccluder2D that remains on default for occluder_light_mask and light_mask (layer 1)
4. have the LightOccluder2D polygon cover (part of) the sprite
5. hit F6 and note that the shadow is rendered on top of the sprite. the shadow should not be rendered on top of the sprite as is the case in Godot 3.

### Minimal reproduction project

projects for both godot 3 and 4 to compare:

[light-occluder-sprite-bug.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/9435066/light-occluder-sprite-bug.zip)
comments: In godot3, add a CanvasModulate node, and then a PointLight2d node. Set the CanvasModulate color to black and the light will illuminate things in range, this doesn't work in godot4. The documentation is also not updated and the 2D lights don't seem to be maintained!

> In godot3, add a CanvasModulate node, and then a PointLight2d node. Set the CanvasModulate color to black and the light will illuminate things in range, this doesn't work in godot4. The documentation is also not updated and the 2D lights don't seem to be maintained!

Do you have a background set in your Godot 4 scene? I'm able to use the CanvasModulate node fine.

As for documentation, I think that comprehensive Godot 4 docs are still a ways off since the version is still in the early beta phase.

For anyone interested, I'm working around this by : 1. Following the steps above for the bug. 2. Adding an extra light with Shadows disabled and the Item Cull Mask only set on 2 (Layer 2 is the layer of the sprite's light mask). 3. Setting the `range_item_cull_mask` for the original light to only include 1 (Layer 1 is the layer of the occluder's light masks). This is what it looks like: Scene tree:

Has there been any more attention paid to this issue since 4.0 released?  The way light occluders now always draw atop the related sprite has rendered occluders practically unusable in almost every common use case I can think of.

If a tree can't cast a shadow without that shadow obscuring the tree itself, then there's no way to make shadows at all, as far as I can tell.

We discussed this last night in our weekly rendering meeting. 

I think the OP is a bit misleading as it mentions the light_mask and occluder_light_mask, but the problem doesn't really have to do with the occluder. The occluder is already properly culled if its mask doesn't match that of the light (as pointed out by Guilleatm: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/64939#issuecomment-1746001630). The issue is with the Light2D's `shadow_item_cull_mask` and the CanvasItem's `light_mask`. The documentation is also wrong in this regard. 

The problem is that in Godot 3.x, CanvasItems additionally took the occluder_light_mask into account. This worked very simply in 3.x because we did a separate draw call for each light for each draw command. We could then easily filter out the shadow at the same time we filtered out the light. 

In 4.x, we render all lights in the same draw call. Which means if we want to bring back that behaviour, we need to mask out the shadow in the shader
